Job Requirements

Engineering Manager - Digital Backbone

Role purpose: Build the teams, engineering system, and leadership capability that turn Digital Backbone into the reusable, trusted foundation for Siemens Healthineers' next generations of connected, cloud-ready, AI-enabled healthcare products. The role combines people leadership, product-minded engineering management, and cross-organization influence to convert platform strategy into measurable customer, business, and engineering outcomes. 

What Digital Backbone Is

Digital Backbone is the common digital and engineering foundation that connects products, services, data, devices, and clinical workflows across Digital & Automation. It provides reusable platform capabilities for cloud, edge, and on-premises deployments so business lines can innovate faster without repeatedly rebuilding infrastructure, integration, deployment, data, fleet, licensing, observability, and workflow capabilities. Its value is not measured only by platform delivery, but by the speed, quality, reuse, interoperability, and new business outcomes it enables across the Siemens Healthineers ecosystem. 

What Digital Backbone Must Enable In The Coming Years

- One engineering foundation across deployment models: enable containerized components and consistent development, integration, release, and operation across cloud, edge, and on-premises environments. 
 - Reusable platform products at enterprise scale: shift from local solutions to governed capabilities that multiple business lines can discover, adopt, integrate, and evolve. 
 - Connected and interoperable healthcare ecosystems: strengthen common services for clinical information exchange, workflow orchestration, fleet and device connectivity, deployment, data, analytics, licensing, and business operations. 
 - AI-ready and AI-native healthcare engineering: provide safe, auditable foundations for AI-enabled workflows while embedding responsible AI into the software lifecycle, engineering knowledge, quality, and productivity. 
 - Faster customer value and new business models: shorten time-to-market, decouple software development from delivery, expand fleet-wide services, and enable subscription, metering, marketplace, and data-driven offerings. 
 - Operational trust at scale: make reliability, cybersecurity, privacy, regulatory evidence, observability, supportability, and lifecycle sustainability intrinsic platform qualities. 
 - A product-oriented global operating model: create clear end-to-end ownership, transparent priorities, strong domain leadership, and accountable collaboration across product, engineering, architecture, quality, and business stakeholders. 

Engineering Manager Mission

Create an environment in which autonomous, inclusive, high-performing teams deliver dependable platform products and continuously increase their impact across Digital & Automation. The Engineering Manager owns the health and capability of the engineering organization: the right people, skills, ways of working, quality discipline, delivery system, and partnerships needed to scale Digital Backbone outcomes. 

Core Accountabilities

- Translate strategy into team outcomes: connect Siemens Healthineers, Digital & Automation, BTT, platform, and product priorities to clear team objectives, roadmaps, technical investments, and measurable outcomes. 
 - Own organizational capability: build balanced teams, identify future skill needs, develop succession, grow technical and people leaders, and enable mobility across products, domains, and geographies. 
 - Lead predictable value delivery: establish outcome-based planning, dependency and risk management, transparent flow metrics, and effective collaboration across teams without reducing agility to ceremony compliance. 
 - Drive engineering excellence: improve architecture realization, software craftsmanship, automation, CI/CD, test strategy, cybersecurity, reliability, observability, maintainability, and lifecycle cost. 
 - Scale platform adoption and reuse: treat internal consumers as customers, reduce onboarding friction, actively manage feedback, avoid duplicate solutions, and make reusable capabilities the preferred path. 
 - Lead responsible AI transformation: model effective AI use, establish human validation and governance, develop AI-native skills, and convert successful experiments into reusable engineering practices and product value. 
 - Manage end-to-end ownership: ensure teams understand and own build, release, operation, support, quality, and improvement of their platform products throughout the lifecycle. 
 - Shape cross-functional decisions: partner with Product Managers, Architects, System Engineers, Quality, Cybersecurity, Operations, and business lines to resolve trade-offs and align investment with enterprise value. 
 - Build a trusted culture: create psychological safety, high standards, inclusion, accountability, candid feedback, and space for experimentation and learning. Promote and protect Peakon participation and leverage it as strategic tool for employee engagement. 
 - Represent engineering: communicate progress, risks, options, and impact in business language; influence priorities and secure the decisions, funding, and staffing needed for sustainable outcomes. 

Role Boundaries and Key Partnerships

The Engineering Manager is accountable for people, engineering capability, delivery health, and the environment in which technical decisions are executed. Product Managers own product value, priorities, and market outcomes; Architects own architectural direction and integrity; technical leaders guide implementation and engineering practices. The Engineering Manager connects these accountabilities, makes ownership explicit, removes systemic barriers, and ensures decisions become dependable outcomes rather than parallel plans. 

Measures of Success

- Accountability: the degree to which the engineering manager can create accountability amongst developers and team leadership acting as the anchor for stability and transparency. 
 - Customer and ecosystem impact: adoption, active consumers, integration lead time, reuse, customer outcomes, and satisfaction of internal and external partners. 
 - Delivery performance: predictable commitments, shorter lead time, improved flow, controlled dependencies, and faster recovery from issues. 
 - Engineering quality: automation, defect escape rate, reliability, security posture, observability, maintainability, and reduced technical debt or lifecycle cost. 
 - AI and modernization impact: measured productivity and quality gains, reusable AI-enabled workflows, responsible adoption, and migration from legacy approaches. 
 - People and capability: critical-skill coverage, internal growth, leadership pipeline, engagement, inclusion, retention, and evidence-based development. 
 - Business contribution: avoided duplication, lower cost to serve, faster time-to-market, platform-enabled revenue opportunities, and progress against strategic targets. 

What Makes This Role Exciting

This is an opportunity to shape how future healthcare software is built and delivered-not only to manage an existing team. data.title: Python Fullstack Engineer
data.description:
Full-Stack Engineer (Mid-Seniority)

Work Model: Remote

Employment Type: Full-time

Reports To: Engineering Lead

Experience: 5-7 years

About the Role

We're looking for a Full-Stack Engineer to design, build, and run production features across our platform, using the ReactJs and Python services and PostgreSQL data behind it. 

You'll own features end to end: shaping the technical approach with Product, writing the API and UI, shipping through CI/CD, and staying accountable once the feature is in front of real users. You'll work in a codebase where REST APIs and microservices coexist, performance and reliability matter, and engineers debug their own code in production rather than throwing it over the wall. 

What You'll Do

• Build and ship full-stack features in TypeScript across ReactJs/Next. js frontends & Python backends. 

• Design and implement REST APIs with clear contracts, versioning, validation, and error handling that other teams can build against without guesswork. 

• Build frontend components that stay fast and maintainable as the product grows, with attention to state management, rendering performance, and accessibility. 

• Model data in PostgreSQL: write efficient queries, design schemas and migrations that don't lock tables in production, and use Redis for caching where it earns its complexity. 

• Take part in system design for new services and features, weighing trade-offs between simplicity, scalability, and delivery time, and documenting decisions. 

• Write unit, integration, and end-to-end tests that catch real regressions, and keep the CI pipeline fast and trustworthy. 

• Review code with a focus on correctness, readability, and long-term maintainability; raise the team's quality bar through feedback, not gatekeeping. 

• Instrument services with logs, metrics, and traces so issues can be diagnosed quickly; participate in on-call and incident reviews [if required can do the on-call expectation]. 

• Find and fix performance bottlenecks across the stack, from slow queries and N+1 calls to oversized bundles and unnecessary re-renders. 

• Work closely with Product, Design, QA, and DevOps to scope work realistically, surface risks early, and deliver incrementally. 

What We're Looking For

Required

• 5-7 years of professional software engineering experience, with a meaningful share spent building and running production web applications. 

• Solid experience with TypeScript/JavaScript and React (Next. js or Angular also valued). 

• Backend experience with Python and preferred Node. js, including building and maintaining REST APIs. 

• Working knowledge of relational databases, preferably PostgreSQL: schema design, indexing, query tuning. 

• Habitual use of automated testing at multiple levels, and comfort working in a Git-based CI/CD workflow. 

• Real production experience: you've debugged issues from logs and metrics, handled an incident, and fixed root causes rather than symptoms. 

• System design ability appropriate to midlevel, you can break down an ambiguous feature into components, APIs, and data models and explain the trade-offs. 

• Clear written and verbal communication with both engineers and non-engineers. 

Nice to Have

• Experience deploying and operating services on AWS or Azure, using Docker and Kubernetes. 

• Experience with distributed systems, microservices, or event-driven architectures (queues, pub/sub). 

• Hands-on use of Redis or messaging systems in production. 

• Background in FinTech or Digital Commerce, especially payments, transactions, or high-traffic checkout flows. 

• Experience integrating LLMs or Generative AI features into products, or using AI-assisted development tools effectively and critically. 

What Success Looks Like

• Within your first 7 days, you're independently delivering features from design through production with minimal hand-holding. 

• Your technical decisions hold up: designs are documented, trade-offs are explicit, and your code needs few follow-up fixes. 

• Services and features you own show measurable improvement in reliability or performance (e. g. , lower error rates, faster p95 latency, fewer incidents). 

• You own your systems in production: you're the first to notice when something breaks and the one who makes sure it doesn't happen again. 

• Product, QA, and DevOps partners describe you as someone who flags risks early and makes delivery more predictable. 

• Your reviews, documentation, and pairing make the engineers around you more effective.

data.title: Software Engineer II (JVM)
data.description:
Nexla, briefly

Nexla is the data layer for enterprise AI. We give AI apps and agents the connectivity, context, and governance to work across more than 1, 000 enterprise systems in real time, and we process over a trillion records a month doing it. DoorDash, LinkedIn, Johnson & Johnson, Instacart, and LiveRamp run mission-critical data on us. Honorable Mention in the Gartner Magic QuadrantTM for Data Integration Tools, and top-rated by customers on Gartner Peer Insights four years running. Founded 2016, remote-first, headquartered in San Mateo. 

Our values are short and we actually use them: Have Empathy. Be Curious. Be Intellectually Honest. Achieve Excellence. Remember to Relax. 

Role

You would work on the backend systems that move data through Nexla: JVM services, the streaming runtime on Kafka, and the distributed processing underneath it. Production Java every day. You take a problem, shape the design, build it, and own it through deploy and on-call. You debug it when it breaks. Small, focused team, which is why the ownership is real rather than nominal. This role sits closest to the integration layer, where the platform meets everything outside it, so the problem below is the one you would live in. 

What you'll own

- Core framework features, designed and shipped by you. Schema evolution, pagination, rate limiting, circuit breaking, and the automated retries and self-recovery that keep pipelines running without a human watching. The SDKs and interfaces other teams build on sit here too: you write them, document them, and use them yourself. 
 - The streaming and processing path in production. Kafka, Spark, and Flink workloads, checkpointing, backpressure, and failure recovery. You operate what you build. 
 - Design decisions inside your scope, and a real voice in the ones above it. Multi-tenancy, concurrency, and latency show up in almost everything here, and you would be expected to have views on the tradeoffs rather than only implementing someone else's. 
 - The hard debugging. Trace failures across Kafka clusters, distributed runtimes, and flaky third-party APIs, fix them, then build the guardrails so they do not come back. 

Roughly 70% building and shipping, 15% design and technical discussion, 15% code review and the RFCs, runbooks, and docs that come with it. 

The hard problem

Our platform integrates with more than a thousand external systems, each with its own schema quirks, auth scheme, rate limits, and retry semantics. The framework problem is the N+1 one: making the thousandth integration as cheap to add as the tenth. That means absorbing the differences into the abstraction rather than special-casing them, while the data underneath keeps moving at production volume. 

Must-Haves

- 5 to 8 years of software engineering, with some of it on backend platforms, services, or SDKs rather than only end-user applications. 
 - Strong Java. You understand JVM memory management, concurrency models, and non-blocking I/O, and you can work your way to the cause of a thread starvation issue from a heap dump. 
 - Hands-on experience with distributed systems in production: Kafka, Spark, Flink, or similar. You have run them, not only built against them. 
 - Comfort with the modern data stack and the protocols around it: Snowflake, Databricks, gRPC, GraphQL, webhooks, and CDC. 
 - You have owned production systems and know what good operational discipline looks like. 
 - You use AI tools in your actual work and can say specifically where they help and where they mislead you. 

Bonus points

- Contributions to open-source data projects such as Airbyte, Flink, Debezium, or Arrow. 
 - Time at an iPaaS or ELT company: MuleSoft, Fivetran, Informatica, Airbyte, or similar. 
 - Deep Kubernetes and cloud-native experience, including Strimzi for Kafka. 
 - Security architecture: OAuth 2. 0, mTLS, and encrypted credential management at scale. 

You'll thrive here if

- You want ownership and will take it. You write code every day and you carry what you ship, through deploy and on-call. 
 - You are comfortable defining scope on the fly and shipping before the full picture is clear. 
 - You would rather build the guardrail than fix the same failure twice. 
 - You raise the quality of what is around you through review and pairing, not just the quality of what you write yourself. 

One thing to be clear about: our product definition is still moving as AI reshapes data integration, and the platform has to move with it. If you want a stable, well-defined surface to work on, this is not it. 

How We Hire

Four conversations, about two weeks end to end. 

- Coding. Working through real code rather than a puzzle. 
 - Low-level design. How you structure a system at the class and interface level, and the tradeoffs you would defend. 
 - High-level design. Distributed systems design on a problem close to what we run in production. 
 - Hiring Manager. Ownership, clarity of thinking, and how you actually use AI in your work. 

On AI in the coding round. Use it the way you would on the job, ours or anyone else's. We build AI tooling and we expect you to use AI tooling, so watching you work without it would tell us nothing useful. What we dig into is your judgment: what you delegated, what you verified, and what you threw away. 

You will hear from us either way. 

The practical stuff

Bengaluru, hybrid, 2 days a week in office. Compensation includes base salary and equity, set by depth and experience rather than by title. You will need to overlap with morning Pacific hours for syncs, design reviews, and collaboration with our US-based leadership and engineering teams. 

Worth a look before you apply

- What we are building now. MCP Studio and Express, our two newest bets. 
 - Who uses us, and why. nexla. com/customers
 - The product in engineer terms. docs. nexla. com
 - Our CEO on why we take "Remember to Relax" seriously. Read the founder story
 - Everything else. nexla. com
 - Blog
 - All open roles

Why Nexla? Why now?

A few large companies - DoorDash, SentinelOne, Johnson & Johnson, LinkedIn, Amex, Integrity Marketing, among them use Nexla for data integration. Connectors, runtime, transformations, scheduling, the parts of the stack where data has to move between systems reliably. 

The reason this is an interesting moment to join is what the agent shift is doing to the category. Data integration used to mean "land this data in that warehouse so a human can look at it. " That product is mature. What it's becoming is closer to "an agent asks a business question, and the platform figures out which data and what code and which APIs add up to a real answer. " That's a much bigger problem, and most of the architecture for it hasn't been built yet by anyone. 

A concrete example. A revenue team wants to ask "which enterprise customers are showing renewal risk" and get a real answer through whatever agent or app they work in. Today there is no clean way to answer that question, it requires CRM, usage, support, and billing data joined in org-specific ways, and the calling agent can't just invoke a tool that returns the right answer unless someone first establishes whether the underlying data is even capable of producing one. 

That is the system we are building. A probe agent investigates the data plane whether the right fields are populated, whether freshness is adequate, whether the joins exist, whether credentials cover the required scope and returns a grounded feasibility answer. Where there are gaps, Express. dev composes the pipelines to close them. The capability is then exposed as an MCP server: "renewal risk" as a curated product, with the business logic correct and the query semantics described well enough that the calling agent uses it as intended. The MCP Gateway governs which agents can call which capabilities, with the policies, audit, and observability an enterprise control plane requires. 

The bet is that ten years of connector work, an enterprise customer base, and a runtime that already moves real volume are the right foundation to define this layer from.

You would not own this problem on your own, but you would be working on pieces of it from early on. 

Must-Haves

- 2 to 5 years of professional software engineering, with Java as your primary language. 
 - Solid JVM fundamentals: collections, concurrency basics, how memory behaves, and enough to read a stack trace or a thread dump when something is wrong. 
 - You write tests as part of building, not after someone asks for them. 
 - Comfortable with SQL, and with at least one of the protocols the platform speaks: gRPC, REST, webhooks, or CDC. 
 - You use AI tools in your actual work and can say specifically where they help and where they mislead you. 

Bonus points

- Exposure to Kafka, Spark, Flink, or a similar distributed system in production, even if you were not the one running it. 
 - Kubernetes, or any experience debugging something that was not running on your laptop. 
 - Open-source contributions, side projects, or anything you have built that you can walk us through. 
 - Data integration, ETL, or any work that involved cleaning up someone else's messy data. 

You'll thrive here if

- You finish things. Started and done are different, and you know which one you are at. 
 - You ask early when you are stuck, and you have usually tried two things first. 
 - You read code you did not write without complaining about it. 
 - You want to get a lot better quickly, and you would rather have hard feedback than polite feedback. 

One thing to be clear about: our product definition is still moving as AI reshapes data integration, and the platform has to move with it. If you want a stable, well-defined surface to work on, this is not it. 

How We Hire

Four conversations, about two weeks end to end. 

- Coding. Working through real code rather than a puzzle. 
 - Low-level design. How you structure a class or a small system, and why you made those calls. 
 - High-level design. What do you think about a system larger than anything you have built yet. We calibrate this to your experience. 
 - Hiring Manager. How you learn, how you own things, and how you actually use AI in your work. 

On AI in the coding round. Use it the way you would on the job, ours or anyone else's. We build AI tooling and we expect you to use AI tooling, so watching you work without it would tell us nothing useful. What we dig into is your judgment: what you delegated, what you verified, and what you threw away. 

You will hear from us either way. 

The practical stuff

Bengaluru, hybrid, 2 days a week in office. Compensation includes base salary and equity, set by depth and experience rather than by title. You will need to overlap with morning Pacific hours for syncs, design reviews, and collaboration with our US-based leadership and engineering teams. 

Worth a look before you apply

- What we are building now. MCP Studio and Express, our two newest bets. 
 - Who uses us, and why. nexla. com/customers
 - The product in engineer terms. docs. nexla. com
 - Our CEO on why we take "Remember to Relax" seriously. Read the founder story
 - Everything else. nexla. com
 - Blog
 - All open roles

Why Nexla? Why now?

A few large companies - DoorDash, SentinelOne, Johnson & Johnson, LinkedIn, Amex, Integrity Marketing, among them use Nexla for data integration. Connectors, runtime, transformations, scheduling, the parts of the stack where data has to move between systems reliably. 

The reason this is an interesting moment to join is what the agent shift is doing to the category. Data integration used to mean "land this data in that warehouse so a human can look at it. " That product is mature. What it's becoming is closer to "an agent asks a business question, and the platform figures out which data and what code and which APIs add up to a real answer. " That's a much bigger problem, and most of the architecture for it hasn't been built yet by anyone. 

A concrete example. A revenue team wants to ask "which enterprise customers are showing renewal risk" and get a real answer through whatever agent or app they work in. Today there is no clean way to answer that question, it requires CRM, usage, support, and billing data joined in org-specific ways, and the calling agent can't just invoke a tool that returns the right answer unless someone first establishes whether the underlying data is even capable of producing one. 

That is the system we are building. A probe agent investigates the data plane whether the right fields are populated, whether freshness is adequate, whether the joins exist, whether credentials cover the required scope and returns a grounded feasibility answer. Where there are gaps, Express. dev composes the pipelines to close them. The capability is then exposed as an MCP server: "renewal risk" as a curated product, with the business logic correct and the query semantics described well enough that the calling agent uses it as intended. The MCP Gateway governs which agents can call which capabilities, with the policies, audit, and observability an enterprise control plane requires. 

The bet is that ten years of connector work, an enterprise customer base, and a runtime that already moves real volume are the right foundation to define this layer from.

Job Description Summary

Responsable de la conception, du développement et du test des logiciels intégrés (micrologiciels), des plates-formes et des systèmes contrôlant et fonctionnant sur des périphériques devant être adaptés aux besoins du matériel qu'ils doivent contrôler et sur lequel ils doivent s'exécuter (c'est-à-dire qui contrôle directement les fonctions en temps réel d'un dispositif physique tel que des moteurs, des alternateurs, des vannes, des ventilateurs et d'autres dispositifs et produits). Cela nécessite généralement une compréhension approfondie des caractéristiques du périphérique physique contrôlé, des fonctions en temps réel qu'il est censé exécuter, ainsi que la capacité de concevoir, de développer, d'implémenter et de tester la logique et les logiciels nécessaires à l'exécution de la fonctionnalité temps réel. Habituellement adapté aux produits et services de divers comptes de résultat. Exerce une influence sur les opérations département et est responsable de la planification et/ou de l'exécution. Ce rôle jouit d'une certaine autonomie, mais est axé sur l'exécution d'activités au sein d'une discipline opérationnelle couverte par les pratiques et procédures fonctionnelles standard. Un certain discernement peut être nécessaire, mais généralement dans le cadre d'une orientation. 

Job Description

Rôles et responsabilités

- Conçoit, design et/ou programme/développe un petit module ou un grand composant, une fonctionnalité, un ensemble de fonctionnalités, une zone de fonctionnalités complète ou un produit logiciel intégré complet. Les domaines d'expertise peuvent inclure, sans toutefois s'y limiter, les réseaux, les systèmes d'exploitation, la cybersécurité, les bases de données ou les applications.  - Fait preuve de discernement et est en capacité de proposer différentes solutions en dehors des paramètres définis, dans le cadre d'une orientation. Se fonde sur une expérience antérieure et la formation professionnelle pour résoudre des tâches simples. Possède les compétences techniques et l'esprit d'analyse nécessaires à la résolution de problèmes. Peut utiliser plusieurs sources internes en dehors de sa propre équipe pour prendre des décisions. 
 - Un poste à ce niveau est susceptible d'être un contributeur individuel, avec des compétences interpersonnelles éprouvées ou un People Leader capable d'embaucher et de développer des talents. Fournit des conseils informels aux nouveaux membres de l'équipe. 

Qualifications De Base

-

Connaissances de niveau équivalent à une licence dans une université accréditée (ou un baccalauréat avec une expérience dans un domaine pertinent). 
 - Pour les rôles aux États-Unis - Licence d'une université accrédité (ou diplôme d'études secondaires et/ou diplôme d'étude général avec au moins 4 ans d'expérience dans la fonction). 

Caractéristiques souhaitées

- Solides compétences en communication orale et écrite. Solides compétences relationnelles et de leadership. Capacité à influencer les autres et à diriger de petites équipes. Mener des initiatives d'envergure et d'impact modérés. Capacité à coordonner plusieurs projets simultanément. Identification efficace des problèmes et compétences en résolution de problèmes. Capacités d'analyse et d'organisation prouvées. Remarque : Pour se conformer aux exigences légales américaines en matière d'immigration et autres, il est nécessaire de préciser le nombre minimum d'années d'expérience requis pour tout poste basé aux États-Unis. Pour les rôles en dehors des États-Unis, pour assurer la conformité avec la législation applicable, les juristes doivent mentionner le niveau d'expérience requis et non PAS un nombre minimum d'années. Cette description de poste a pour but de fournir un guide détaillé du rôle. Toutefois, il n'est pas prévu de modifier ou de restreindre et/ou d'élargir de quelque manière que ce soit les tâches requises de chaque employé, telles qu'elles sont définies dans leur contrat de travail respectif et/ou convenues d'un commun accord entre un employé et son responsable.

data.title: Engineer, Staff_CE
data.description:
Company

Qualcomm India Private Limited

Job Area

Engineering Group, Engineering Group > Software Applications Engineering

General Summary

JOB OVERVIEW

This position is part of the Qualcomm Customer Engineering Group, which collaborates closely with automotive partners and customers - from concept through commercialization - across Qualcomm's broad Snapdragon Automotive platform portfolio. The team supports all aspects of embedded software including hardware and software architecture, feature bring-up, platform integration, software customization, system validation, and complex debugging efforts that are critical to product launch. 

This is a Staff-level Software Applications Engineering position focused on BSP and HLOS Stability for Qualcomm Snapdragon Automotive platforms. The primary mission of this role is to own, triage, debug, and resolve system stability issues across IVI, ADAS, and FLEX segments for global automotive customers. The role spans multiple OS environments including QNX (HQX) and HGY (Hypervisor Gunyah with Linux/Android GVM), covering both QNX PVM and multi-OS virtualized stacks. 

The successful candidate will serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) for platform stability, driving cross-functional collaboration between the Customer Engineering team, Dev/Platform SW teams, and OEM/Tier-1 customers. As a Staff Engineer, this individual will also provide technical leadership, mentor engineers, define debug methodologies, and contribute to the continuous improvement of stability tools and automation frameworks. 

Key Responsibilities

System Stability - Debugging & Resolution

- Lead triage and root-cause analysis of system stability issues (crashes, hangs, watchdog resets, panics, SOC resets) across QNX (HQX) and HGY (Gunyah) platforms for automotive customers. 
 - Debug kernel crashes, process crashes, resource-manager failures, and OS-level hangs on QNX IVI, ADAS, and FLEX variants. 
 - Analyze full ramdumps, minidumps, and guest-dumps (QNX/Android/Linux GVM) using Crashscope, QXDM, QDSS traces, and other Qualcomm diagnostic toolchains. 
 - Identify, isolate, and drive resolution of stability regressions across chipset generations (Gen3, Gen4, Gen4. 5, Gen5) on both HQX and HGY stacks. 
 - Own stability-related Change Requests (CRs) end-to-end - from initial triage through root-cause analysis, patch validation, and integration into customer branches. 
 - Collaborate with Dev/PLT teams to diagnose Linux kernel panics, Android GVM crashes, and Gunyah hypervisor-level faults within the HGY multi-OS virtualized stack.

Customer Engagement & Technical Support

data.title: Principal AI Engineer
data.description:
TechGrove is the Centre of Excellence for Banyan Software, based in Chennai, India. It plays a key role in supporting Banyan's global businesses through technology, security, and software development. TechGrove brings together India's deep pool of technical talent with Banyan's long-term approach to growth, creating a trusted, developer-focused environment where people can do their best work. 

About Berkeley Myles
We build software for UK manufacturers who can't afford to get things wrong: aerospace, medical  devices, oil and gas, motorsport. Our product, ProgressPlus, runs the whole job from first enquiry  through to final invoice. Hundreds of manufacturers run on it every day, and when one of them has to  prove what went into a part, it's where the answer comes from. We're now building a new product with  AI on every stage of that flow. 
We're part of Banyan Software, the best permanent home for software businesses that serve  specialised industries, their employees, and their customers. Banyan is a Great Place to Work Certified  company, a five-time Inc. 5000 honoree, and a top-10 company on the Deloitte Technology Fast 500. 
Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Atlanta, Banyan operates more than 100 portfolio companies  across North America, the UK, the EU, and APAC. 

About the Role
A manufacturer runs one flow: enquiry, quote, order, jobs, scheduling, tracking, quality, shipping,   invoice. ProgressPlus is the system of record for that flow. We're building the system of action on top of
it: AI that works on every stage, capturing enquiries, validating orders, optimising schedules,   anticipating problems, and reconciling invoices, always with a human in control and every step
auditable.   You'll be the company's first AI engineer. There's not much AI in production today: no agents, no  runtime, no AI layer. You'll build the system of action from a blank page. It has two parts: the events that  announce what just happened in the business, and the agents that act on them. Agents that plan multi-  step work, run in the background, act under their own identity with bounded authority, and leave a trail a  regulated manufacturer can show an auditor.   The ground is prepared. Five . NET services with architecture boundaries enforced in CI, and a growing  catalog of transaction-safe business operations ready to become AI tools. This is a founding role: you  set the architecture, the standards and the evaluation discipline that every AI feature in this product gets  built on. 

Key Responsibilities
Build the agentic layer: one coherent layer that every AI capability in the product runs on. Once it exists,   adding AI to any stage of the manufacturing flow is a few weeks of feature work. 
The runtime and the tools  Architect the agent runtime: a server-side loop with durable runs, retries, scheduled and event-driven  triggers, and human-in-the-loop steps
Build the tool layer that turns our catalog of transaction-safe business operations into typed, tenant-  scoped, permissioned AI tools, for our own agents and for the outside world through MCP
Evaluation and audit  Make evals part of how we ship: fixture-based tests of every AI behaviour, wired into CI from day one  Close the correction loop: every override, rejection and edit captured as structured signal, so evals  and retrieval improve from real use  Build agent auditing into the platform's tamper-evident action log as it lands: every agent step  logged, attributable and replayable. Our customers pass AS9100 audits, and explainable AI is a
feature we sell  Grounding and operations  Drive the event catalog: which business facts the product announces, from the office to the shop  floor (SalesOrderCreated, GoodsReceived, JobRunningLate). Every agent run starts from one  Grow the semantic grounding: a machine-readable model of the business and how it fits together, so  agents retrieve facts instead of inventing them
Own the agent authority model: what an agent may do, its budget, how much autonomy each  workflow gets. Instrument the runtime so every step is metered and traced
Run what you ship: your agents in production are yours, including the incident when one misbehaves

What Success Looks Like
First three months: one real workflow runs end to end on the agent runtime in production, with its  evals in CI and every step in the audit log. 
First six months: more agents are live on the same layer, and at least one of them was built by one  of the full stack engineers. 
First twelve months: adding AI to a stage of the flow is a few weeks of feature work for any  engineer here, and you can show an auditor how any of it reached the answer it did. 

How We Work
Linear as the single board: work traced from issue to acceptance criteria to PR, reporting as a by-  product of the work
A small team: full stack engineers with a lead, plus AI and platform specialists, on a . NET and Next. js  platform on Azure  Prototype-led: we design the flow before we build it, against a shared design system
AI in daily use across the team: coding agents in the repo with the context they need, and AI tooling
for research, prototyping and analysis
A customer base we can pick up the phone to, and an implementation team on their sites every week

Tech Stack You'll Use
Backend: C#, . NET 10, Rebus messaging, SQL Server (database per company)
Frontend: Next. js, React, TypeScript
Cloud: Azure (Container Apps, Azure SQL, Service Bus, Front Door), Bicep, GitHub Actions
AI: Model-agnostic by design, with MCP as the tool protocol
Tooling: Claude Code, Linear, GitHub

What We're Looking For      
You've taken multiple LLM-powered systems from prototype to production, at least one of them  agentic (multi-step, tool-using, running unattended), and you can walk us through what broke and
what you'd redo  Product instincts and a builder's disposition: you can sit with a planner or a quoting manager,   translate their workflow into an agent architecture without being handed a spec, then write the code, 
ship it, and talk to the people who use it  Strong backend and systems engineering experience (5+ years). You've built event-driven systems, 
you can explain why the transactional outbox exists, and you think in contracts, idempotency and  failure modes
You treat evals and observability as part of the definition of done, and you've wired LLM evaluation  and observability tooling
You treat AI security as an engineering problem: injection containment, retrieved content handled  strictly as data, and hostile inputs in the eval suite
Clear opinions on build versus buy: you know which parts of an agent stack to take from providers  and which parts you have to own
Comfortable being first: setting standards, writing them down, and reviewing others' work against  them
Strong written communication: you'll work with a team split across time zones
Preferred Experience
You've shipped something in manufacturing, ERP, supply chain or industrial operations, or you're  genuinely curious about how factories run
Document extraction pipelines: structured extraction from PDFs and email, OCR cascades,   confidence-scored human review

  

Recruitment Notice

TechGrove may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to assist in screening and/or assessing applicants during the recruitment process. All hiring decisions are made by our team. Personal information submitted through your application will be collected and used for recruitment purposes in accordance with applicable privacy laws. Contact us at any time with questions about our process or to request accommodation. 

Beware of Recruitment Scams

We have been made aware of individuals fraudulently posing as members of our Talent Acquisition team and extending fake job offers. These scams may involve requests for personal information or payment for equipment.   

Protect yourself by following these steps: 

- Verify that all communications from our recruiting team come from an @banyansoftware. com email address. 
 - Remember, employers will never request payment or banking information during the hiring process. 
 - If you receive a suspicious message, do not respond - instead, forward it to careers@banyansoftware. com and/or report it to the platform where you received it. Your safety and security are important to us. Thank you for staying vigilant.

NTT DATA strives to hire exceptional, innovative and passionate individuals who want to grow with us. If you want to be part of an inclusive, adaptable, and forward-thinking organization, apply now. 

We are currently seeking a Testing Engineering Senior Specialist to join our team in Noida, Uttar Pradesh (IN-UP), India (IN). 

Coding Language - Java Primary, Python Good to have

 - 5+ years in a Test Architect, Solution Architect, QE Architect, Technical Lead, or equivalent technical leadership role. 

Job Description - API Test Architect & Test Solution Lead

API Modernization | Microservices | Healthcare | Quality Engineering

Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced API Test Architect & Solution Lead to lead the quality engineering strategy, architecture, and implementation for large-scale API modernization and microservices transformation programs within the healthcare domain. 

The role will be responsible for defining the end-to-end API testing architecture and modernization validation strategy for enterprise services being transformed from legacy/monolithic platforms into modern RESTful APIs and microservices. 

This is a customer-facing technical leadership role requiring strong expertise in API testing, test automation architecture, microservices, legacy-to-modern API parity validation, CI/CD integration, healthcare data validation, and AI-assisted Quality Engineering. 

The Solution Lead will work closely with enterprise architects, API developers, product owners, business teams, DevOps teams, and QA engineering teams to ensure modernized services meet functional, integration, data integrity, performance, security, and release-readiness requirements. 

Key Responsibilities

API Test Architecture & Solutioning

- Define the enterprise API Quality Engineering architecture, strategy, standards, and implementation roadmap for API modernization programs. 
 - Design scalable and reusable API automation frameworks supporting hundreds of APIs and thousands of test scenarios. 
 - Establish standardized testing approaches using Cucumber, TestNG, REST Assured, Gradle, Git/Bitbucket, Jenkins/Udeploy, and automated reporting. 
 - Define framework architecture with clear separation of: 
 - Test data
 - Test logic
 - Configuration
 - Validation utilities
 - Reporting
 - Environment management
 - Build reusable automation components, utilities, libraries, and common validation capabilities that can be adopted across multiple projects. 
 - Establish traceability across requirements → feature files → test data → automated execution → defects → results. 

API Modernization & Microservices Validation

- Lead testing strategy for migration of legacy enterprise services to REST APIs and microservices architecture. 
 - Define legacy-versus-modernized service parity testing to ensure business functionality and data behavior remain consistent during modernization. 
 - Establish baseline request/response datasets from legacy services and compare them against modernized API responses. 
 - Design automated comparison capabilities for: 
 - Request/response validation
 - JSON/XML payload comparison
 - Schema validation
 - Field-level comparison
 - Business-rule validation
 - Data transformation validation
 - Database/backend validation
 - Error and exception handling
 - Validate service decomposition and interactions across distributed microservices. 
 - Develop testing approaches for synchronous and asynchronous service integrations. 
 - Define regression strategies that allow modernization teams to continuously verify functional parity during incremental migration. 

API Functional & Integration Testing

- Define comprehensive API testing coverage including: 
 - Functional testing
 - Integration testing
 - Contract testing
 - Schema validation
 - Positive and negative testing
 - Boundary testing
 - Authentication and authorization validation
 - Error handling
 - Data integrity validation
 - Regression testing
 - End-to-end service validation
 - Establish API test scenarios based on OpenAPI/Swagger specifications, GraphQL schemas, interface contracts, business requirements, and legacy system documentation. 
 - Define reusable test-data strategies using Excel, generated datasets, synthetic data, and approved production-like samples. 
 - Drive automation-first testing while identifying scenarios requiring specialized or exploratory validation. 

Healthcare Domain Validation

- Provide Quality Engineering leadership for healthcare enterprise services supporting areas such as: 
 - Member and eligibility
 - Provider
 - Claims
 - Benefits
 - Enrollment
 - Accumulators
 - Authorization
 - Payments
 - Clinical and administrative integrations
 - Ensure modernization testing validates critical healthcare business rules and cross-system data integrity. 
 - Support testing of healthcare interoperability and data exchange services where applicable, including FHIR/HL7-based APIs and healthcare integration patterns. 
 - Ensure appropriate handling of sensitive healthcare test data and alignment with organizational security, privacy, and compliance requirements. 

Automation Framework Engineering

- Architect and enhance BDD-based API automation frameworks using: 
 - Cucumber
 - TestNG
 - REST Assured
 - Java
 - Gradle
 - Define reusable feature files, step definitions, API clients, assertion libraries, data utilities, and comparison utilities. 
 - Develop configurable validation mechanisms capable of supporting different APIs without extensive custom coding. 
 - Establish coding standards, framework governance, peer reviews, and reusable engineering patterns. 
 - Optimize automation suites for parallel execution, maintainability, stability, and faster regression cycles. 

CI/CD & DevOps Integration

- Integrate API automation into Jenkins/Udeploy CI/CD pipelines. 
 - Define automated quality gates for builds and deployments. 
 - Enable API regression suites to execute across development, QA, integration, staging, and release environments. 
 - Establish mechanisms for: 
 - Pipeline-triggered execution
 - Environment configuration
 - Test-data management
 - Parallel execution
 - Failure diagnostics
 - Automated reporting
 - Partner with DevOps and engineering teams to enable continuous testing and shift-left quality engineering. 

Reporting & Quality Metrics

- Define enterprise-level API Quality Engineering reporting using: 
 - Cucumber Reports
 - JSON Reports
 - HTML Reports
 - Execution Logs
 - CI/CD dashboards
 - Establish metrics for: 
 - API automation coverage
 - Functional coverage
 - Regression coverage
 - Pass/fail trends
 - Defect leakage
 - Modernization parity
 - Execution stability
 - Release readiness
 - Provide technical insights and quality recommendations to engineering leadership and customer stakeholders. 

AI-Assisted Quality Engineering

- Drive adoption of GitHub Copilot and GenAI-assisted engineering across the API testing lifecycle. 
 - Use AI assistance for: 
 - Requirement and API specification analysis
 - Test scenario generation
 - Test case generation
 - Gherkin/feature-file generation
 - REST Assured automation development
 - Code refactoring
 - Test-data generation
 - Coverage-gap identification
 - Failure analysis
 - Leverage OpenAPI specifications, GraphQL schemas, legacy documentation, and existing test assets as inputs for AI-assisted test design. 
 - Define appropriate human review and governance practices for AI-generated test assets. 
 - Identify opportunities to improve engineering productivity through intelligent automation and reusable accelerators. 

Technical Leadership & Customer Engagement

- Act as the technical solution lead and architecture point of contact for API Quality Engineering. 
 - Engage with customer stakeholders to understand modernization objectives, current-state architecture, quality risks, and target-state requirements. 
 - Translate business and technical requirements into testing architecture, solution approach, implementation roadmap, effort estimates, and delivery plans. 
 - Conduct architecture reviews and technical solution presentations with customers and engineering leadership. 
 - Lead technical discussions across development, architecture, DevOps, business, and QA teams. 
 - Mentor automation engineers and QA leads and provide technical direction across distributed teams. 
 - Identify testing risks, dependencies, technical constraints, and mitigation strategies early in the modernization lifecycle. 

Required Technical Skills

API & Microservices: REST APIs, RESTful services, Microservices Architecture, JSON, XML, OpenAPI/Swagger, GraphQL, API contracts, service integration patterns

API Automation: REST Assured, Cucumber BDD, TestNG, Java, Gradle

Framework Architecture: Reusable automation framework design, modular architecture, custom assertion utilities, schema validation, response comparison, test-data management

DevOps: Jenkins, Udeploy, Git, Bitbucket, CI/CD integration, continuous testing

Testing: API functional testing, integration testing, contract testing, regression testing, legacy-to-modern API parity testing, data validation, negative testing

Reporting: Cucumber Reports, JSON/HTML reporting, execution logs and CI/CD quality reporting

AI-Assisted Engineering: GitHub Copilot, AI-assisted test analysis, scenario generation, Gherkin generation, automation development and coverage analysis

Healthcare: Strong understanding of healthcare enterprise systems and preferably experience with claims, member, provider, eligibility, benefits, authorization, payments, or healthcare interoperability services. 

Preferred Skills

- Experience leading enterprise API modernization or monolith-to-microservices transformation programs. 
 - Experience architecting API automation frameworks used across multiple applications or programs. 
 - Experience with legacy-to-modern service comparison/parity validation. 
 - Knowledge of cloud-native architectures, containers, Kubernetes, API gateways, and service discovery is desirable. 
 - Exposure to service virtualization, mocking, contract testing, and API performance testing. 
 - Knowledge of healthcare interoperability standards such as FHIR and HL7 is advantageous. 
 - Experience implementing AI/GenAI-assisted Quality Engineering practices. 
 - Strong customer-facing solutioning, architecture presentation, estimation, and stakeholder-management capabilities. 

Experience

- 13+ years of overall experience in Quality Engineering, testing, software engineering, or related disciplines. 
 - 7+ years of strong API testing and automation experience. 
 - 5+ years in a Test Architect, Solution Architect, QE Architect, Technical Lead, or equivalent technical leadership role. 
 - Demonstrated experience leading complex API modernization, microservices, integration, or digital transformation programs. 
 - Prior experience in healthcare or health insurance programs is strongly preferred. 

Expected Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate should be able to take an enterprise modernization requirement such as: 

Legacy Enterprise Services → Modern APIs → Microservices

and independently define the corresponding: 

Current-State Assessment → Test Strategy → API Test Architecture → Legacy Baseline → Modern API Validation → Automated Parity Testing → CI/CD Integration → Regression Strategy → Quality Gates → Production Readiness

The candidate should combine hands-on API automation architecture expertise with solutioning and customer-facing leadership, rather than functioning only as a test manager or delivery manager.

data.description:
Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95, 000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first - developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact. 

A Day in the Life

The Quality function partners with Research & Development and Operations teams to ensure medical devices are designed, developed, and maintained in compliance with applicable quality system regulations, risk management requirements, and international standards. The team provides quality engineering leadership throughout the product lifecycle, supporting design controls, verification and validation activities, risk management, product transfers, regulatory compliance, and continuous quality improvement initiatives. 

This position is based in Hyderabad, India and follows a Flex work arrangement. No travel is required. 

As a Quality Engineer II, you will provide design quality engineering support for medical device product development and sustaining engineering activities. The role is responsible for facilitating the application of design controls, risk management, design verification and validation, and regulatory compliance activities while partnering with cross-functional teams throughout the product lifecycle. 

Primary Responsibilities

- Review new and modified product design documentation for quality characteristics, including manufacturability, serviceability, testability, reliability, and product requirements. 
 - Ensure product development projects and design changes comply with FDA Quality System Regulations, European Union Medical Device Regulation (EU MDR), and internal quality requirements. 
 - Partner with cross-functional teams to develop and maintain risk management documentation, including Risk Management Plans, Hazard Analyses, Design Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (DFMEA), and Risk Management Reports in accordance with ISO 14971. 
 - Support design verification and validation activities through development and review of plans, protocols, reports, testing strategies, and compliance assessments. 
 - Review Design History Files (DHF) and Technical Files for compliance with applicable regulations, standards, and quality requirements. 
 - Support successful transfer of products into manufacturing through process validation activities, including Process Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (PFMEA), Installation Qualification (IQ), Operational Qualification (OQ), and Performance Qualification (PQ). 
 - Develop quality system templates, training materials, and guidance related to design controls, risk management, quality system regulations, and applicable standards. 
 - Participate in internal and external audits and provide quality engineering guidance across project teams and organizational functions. 

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering with 5+ years of overall experience, including 3+ years of quality engineering experience in medical device, regulated manufacturing, or healthcare industries. 
 - Experience with medical device Design Controls, Risk Management, and product development activities. 
 - Experience supporting ISO 14971 risk management activities, including Risk Management Plans, Hazard Analyses, and Design Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (DFMEA). 
 - Knowledge of FDA Quality System Regulation, ISO 13485, EU MDR, IEC 60601, 21 CFR Part 820, and 21 CFR Part 11. 
 - Experience using statistical tools and methodologies, including Minitab, sampling plans, hypothesis testing, Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), Gauge Repeatability and Reproducibility (GR&R), and related statistical techniques. 

Preferred Qualifications

- ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), Certified Software Quality Engineer (CSQE), or Certified Reliability Engineer (CRE) certification. 
 - ISO 9001 or ISO 13485 Internal Auditor or Lead Auditor certification. 
 - Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification. 
 - Experience with DMAIC or Design for Six Sigma (DFSS)/DMADV methodologies. 
 - Experience acting as a Risk Management or Design Quality subject matter expert within cross-functional product development teams. 

Physical Job Requirements

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this position, but they are not an exhaustive list of all the required responsibilities and skills of this position. 





Recruitment Fraud Alert

Apply only through official Medtronic channels. All legitimate Medtronic recruiting communications come from approved Medtronic platforms and official @medtronic. com email addresses. 

Medtronic will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information (such as bank account or Social Security details) during early stages of the hiring process. Any such requests are not legitimate.

If you have any questions, concerns regarding the authenticity of a communication alleged to have been made by or on behalf of Medtronic, please contact us immediately at AskHR@medtronic. com. 

Benefits & Compensation

Medtronic offers a competitive Salary and flexible Benefits Package

A commitment to our employees lives at the core of our values. We recognize their contributions. They share in the success they help to create. We offer a wide range of benefits, resources, and competitive compensation plans designed to support you at every career and life stage.

Job Description Summary

As a Lead Engineer - Control & Protection at GE Vernova Grid Solutions, you will play a crucial role in designing, implementing, and optimizing protection relay systems for EHV/HV substations considering the safety/quality/Cost/time delivery criteria. Your expertise will ensure the reliability and efficiency of power systems, supporting our global operations across various regions. 

This role involves in leading the secondary engineering activities (Control & Protection, Substation Automation Systems, Interface Engineering, Telecom Requirements & LV Auxiliary Systems for EHV/HV Electrical Substations (AIS / GIS / HVDC / FACTS / STATCOM / Onshore / Offshore / Renewable/etc. , )

The candidate shall execute with association of workgroups, where applicable, in order to meet assigned objectives. In this role, the candidate will work within defined parameters to draw conclusions, apply concepts to issues of moderate complexity, and resolve issues through immediate action or short-term planning. The candidate will work with GSI Global Engineering Center (GSI GEC) to coordinate with the GSI Regions / Business Lines / as per Project requirement. 

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

Specific Role Requirements

- Design and prepare Engineering drawings (SLD/KLD/PSLD/CRP) as per project requirement in anyone of E-CAD Tool (Ex. Engineering Base software/E-Plan/ AutoCAD Electrical/equivalent) for up to 400/765kV Substations. 
 - Design/Review the Substation automation system based on IEC61850 & interconnections. 
 - Review BOQ and Network drawings of PLCC/FOTE engineering and need to interface between CRP & SAS with Telecom Equipment. 
 - Review equipment drawings of major Substation Equipment for AIS / GIS like Circuit breakers, Isolators, Earth switches, CSD, PDM, Transformers/Reactors & associated Conditional Monitoring Devices etc. , 
 - Perform CT and VT and its sizing calculations. 
 - Design and Review the control/Power cable engineering in substations. 
 - Design the LV/LT auxiliary systems for Electrical Substations and interface with the SAS/SCADA. 
 - Perform/review the protection relay application / setting calculations and coordination including tripping analysis. 

Add-on Competency (Optional)

- Renewable project engg i. e. Solar, On-shore / Off-shore Wind, Battery Storage or hybrid. 
 - HVDC/FACTS integrated project applications. 
 - Perform/Review the study on Electrical Power systems and load flow and short circuit studies etc. , 
 - Competency on specialized tools like CANECO, ETAP, DIG Silent or equivalent
 - Working experience in SAS, Database Preparation in the automation/RTU software
 - Review / consolidate the IO Mapping with respect to the scheme drawings/troubleshoot of database issues in SAS system / RTU based system. 
 - Able to work with different make IEDs, Numerical protection relays and BCUs. 

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor's (or) master's degree in electrical engineering. 
 - 8+ years of experience in substation protection relay systems within EHV Electrical Substations, Oil & Gas or Power Transmission industries. 
 - Experience in EPC (Engineering, Procurement, Construction) environments with multidisciplinary teams. 
 - Experience of Secondary(CRP/SAS, Aux Systems, Telecom, Interface) engineering up to 765kV/400kV/220KV and HVDC Substations (AIS/GIS/SOLAR/WIND). 
 - Experience/Knowledge on Relay Testing, Equipment Testing, Control / Protection scheme testing & SAS Commissioning experience (min 1 year) shall be given additional weightage. 

Desired Characteristics

- Strong oral and written communication skills. Strong interpersonal, responsive and supervision skills. Demonstrated ability to evaluate and resolve problems. Demonstrated ability to manage programs / projects. Ability to document, plan, market, and execute programs. Established project management skills. 
 - Fluent in English; additional language (any foreign Language) is a plus. 
 - Willingness to travel internationally as required. 
 - Proven technical leadership in a complex system engineering development environment. 
 - Proactively serves on cross functional leadership teams; self-directed decision-making; Pulls in experts when needed. 

Key Competences

- Technical Expertise: In-depth understanding of substation protection systems, relay technologies, relay tripping philosophies, substation automation systems, Interface Engineering, LV Auxiliary Systems & Telecom Panels. 
 - Project Management: Ability to manage multiple projects, prioritize tasks, and meet deadlines. 
 - Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills for effective customer and team interactions. 
 - Strong leadership, supportive and team coordination abilities to guide and mentor junior engineers. 
 - Problem-Solving: Proficient in identifying issues and implementing effective solutions. 
 - Quality Focus: Commitment to maintaining high standards of quality and compliance. 

Additional Information

Relocation Assistance Provided: Yes

data.description:
Some Careers Open More Doors Than Others. 

If you're looking for a career that will unlock new opportunities, join HSBC and experience the possibilities. Whether you want a career that could take you to the top, or simply take you in an exciting new direction, HSBC offers opportunities, support and rewards that will take you further. 

Business Description

Our GCIO organisation plays a critical role for the bank. This team partners with our businesses to build the platforms, systems, and products that our customers use every day. This team keeps people's money and data safe, and is at the forefront of driving innovation for our businesses, customers, and colleagues. 

Role purpose

The Technology Country Management role is accountable to the Regional CIO for in-country business relationships, execution of global and regional Technology strategy, and management/oversight of local execution, change portfolio, and Technology services within the country. 

This role provides end-to-end leadership across engineering, delivery, governance, regulatory engagement and audit readiness-ensuring Technology outcomes are secure, resilient, compliant, and aligned to business priorities. 

Key Responsibilities

Country Technology leadership & stakeholder management

- Provide in-country oversight and coordination for Technology services and business relationships, managing resources across multiple Technology disciplines. 
 - Act as the senior Technology point of contact for country stakeholders, ensuring priorities, risks, and dependencies are clearly understood and managed. 
 - Attend relevant COO-chaired governance committees, leading key Technology discussions and driving decisions to closure. 

Strategy execution & roadmap ownership

- Drive and implement the Technology strategy defined by the Group CIO, GB/GF CIOs, Technology Function Heads and Regional CIO-translating it into an executable country plan. 
 - Develop and maintain the Country Technology roadmap, covering all relevant GB/GF and Technology Function activities, aligned to business objectives and regulatory expectations. 
 - Ensure local demand is clearly articulated into global portfolios, with the right data to enable prioritisation and investment decisions. 

Regulatory engagement, audit management & control assurance

- Maintain strong relationships with relevant regulators and government stakeholders, supporting the Regional CIO and country leadership in regulatory engagement. 
 - Face regulators as required: present Technology strategy, control posture, resilience, cyber/operational risk management, and remediation progress with clear, evidence-based narratives. 
 - Lead Technology responses to internal audit, external audit, and regulatory examinations: coordinate walkthroughs, evidence packs, management responses, and closure plans. 
 - Ensure audit findings and regulatory observations are remediated on time with clear ownership, milestones, and sustainable control improvements. 

Engineering leadership (Cloud, API, DevSecOps, AI)

- Provide strong engineering oversight across modern technology stacks, including: 

Cloud engineering (architecture, security, resilience, cost governance)

API platforms/integration (design standards, lifecycle management, reliability)

DevSecOps (CI/CD, automated testing, security scanning, policy-as-code, release governance)

AI/ML enablement (responsible adoption, model risk considerations, data controls, secure deployment patterns)

- Ensure engineering practices meet enterprise standards for security-by-design, reliability, observability, and operational resilience. 
 - Oversee application development, remediation, and service management for non GB/GF CIO-owned solutions/services (where applicable). 

Portfolio, programme & project management (large change portfolio)

- Provide management and oversight of the country change portfolio, including prioritisation, sequencing, dependency management, and benefits tracking. 
 - Lead governance for a large portfolio of programmes and projects, ensuring delivery discipline across scope, schedule, budget, risk, and quality. 
 - Drive consistent delivery reporting (RAID, milestones, financials, resource plans) and intervene early to unblock delivery issues. 
 - Ensure change governance supports safe delivery (release controls, change approvals, incident learnings, post-implementation reviews). 

Service management, incident leadership & operational resilience

- Provide full oversight and advice on Technology issues in-country, including resolution of critical incidents and coordination of key deployments. 
 - Own end-to-end development and running of non GB/GF CIO-owned country Technology services, including problem management and change governance to ensure service quality. 
 - Strengthen operational resilience through improved monitoring, capacity planning, DR readiness, and continuous service improvement. 

Financial, resource & people leadership

- Own direct cost and headcount management for country teams, including annual planning and forecasting. 
 - Lead people change activities (including restructuring where required) in partnership with HR and in line with local requirements. 
 - Build a high-performing culture with clear objectives, talent development, and strong accountability. 

Skills And Experience (requirements)

- Senior Technology leadership experience in a regulated environment, with proven delivery of country-level execution and service oversight. 
 - Demonstrated experience facing regulators and managing audit/exam activities, including evidence preparation and remediation closure. 
 - Strong engineering depth across Cloud, APIs, DevSecOps and modern software delivery practices; working knowledge of AI/ML delivery and governance. 
 - Proven capability managing a large portfolio with strong programme and project management discipline (multi-year roadmaps, complex dependencies, multiple stakeholders). 
 - Excellent communication and executive presence-able to translate complex technical topics into clear business and regulatory outcomes. 
 - Strong governance mindset: risk management, control ownership, operational resilience, and service management. 

As an employee, you are required to perform your duties in a professional capacity exercising independent judgement, discretion and decision-making authority in planning, organising, directing work, supervising and appraising the work of team members, as applicable; and taking accountability for delivery outcomes. You will represent the organization with relevant internal and external stakeholders. You will allocate and prioritize work, provide direction and feedback, manage team capacity and leave in line with policy as applicable. 

Pro-Tip: Familiarity with AI-enabled tools is an advantage. 

You'll achieve more at HSBC. 

HSBC is committed to building a culture where all employees are valued, respected and opinions count. We take pride in providing a workplace that fosters continuous professional development, flexible working and opportunities to grow within an inclusive and diverse environment.

data.description:
Organization: 

At CommBank, we never lose sight of the role we play in other people's financial wellbeing. Our focus is to help people and businesses move forward to progress. To make the right financial decisions and achieve their dreams, targets, and aspirations. Regardless of where you work within our organisation, your initiative, talent, ideas, and energy all contribute to the impact that we can make with our work. Together we can achieve great things. 

Job Title: Executive Manager - Technology Modernisation

Location: Bangalore

Business & Team: 

ASB is one of New Zealand's leading banks and a wholly owned subsidiary of the Commonwealth Bank of Australia. This role sits within CBA India and is dedicated to ASB - you will build and lead ASB's India-based engineering capability, working shoulder to shoulder with ASB Technology leaders in NZ. ASB is mid-flight in a generational modernisation of its technology, data and digital estate. The agenda is set and owned by ASB's leadership in New Zealand; India's job is to bring the engineering depth that accelerates it. The portfolio spans migrating the core to SAP TRBK and simplifying the legacy HOST estate, modernising cards across issuing and acquiring, the full payments technology agenda, scaling Pega across decisioning, workflow, lending and financial crime, modernising the data estate onto a cloud data platform, and re-platforming integration. 

Underpinning all of it are CBA Group engineering foundations - cloud-first architecture, Golden Pathways and DevSecOps, automation-first testing, and AI-powered engineering at scale. This is not a support function. It is real engineering accountability, delivered from India. 

You will lead ASB's India-based engineering capability - engineers, platform and architecture specialists, testing, data and delivery talent - organised into squads that sit inside ASB's tribes and into chapters that hold the engineering craft. The teams operate as a genuine extension of ASB, not a resource pool: named outcomes, shared tribe governance and cadence, common engineering standards, and direct partnership with ASB tribe leads, product owners, architecture, risk and operations across both geographies. 

Impact & Contribution: 

As Executive Manager - Technology Modernisation, you lead the India engineering capability that delivers across ASB's modernisation portfolio - SAP TRBK core migration and legacy simplification, Cards Modernisation, the payments technology agenda, and the Pega estate - together with the cloud, integration, data and quality engineering that make them land. You will work in genuine partnership with the ASB New Zealand leaders who own the modernisation agenda, translating their roadmaps into executable engineering plans, mobilising squads inside ASB tribes, setting and holding the engineering bar, and carrying delivery, operational and regulatory risk for what India commits to. 

Success is a world-class engineering capability across these domains - one that measurably accelerates ASB's modernisation journey, delivers to committed timelines, holds the compliance and regulatory bar without exception, takes risk out of complex migrations, and does it at materially better cost. Alongside the immediate commitments, you will build the longer-term edge: automation-first quality engineering, AI-powered engineering, and the engineering depth that lets ASB retire legacy with confidence. 

Roles & Responsibilities: 

- Lead India's engineering capability across core banking, cards, payments, Pega, data and integration, translating ASB New Zealand's modernisation roadmap into clear, sequenced delivery plans with measurable outcomes. 
 - Build outcome-led engineering squads and chapters integrated with ASB tribes, with clear accountability across software, platform, cloud, data and quality engineering. 
 - Set and uphold engineering excellence, embedding cloud-first architecture, API-led and event-driven integration, Golden Pathways, DevSecOps, CI/CD automation, security controls and measurable engineering standards. 
 - Make automation and quality engineering a core strength, establishing reusable test frameworks and large-scale migration testing to reduce manual regression, accelerate delivery and protect customer outcomes. 
 - Drive major modernisation programmes, including SAP TRBK core migration, legacy HOST transformation, Cards Modernisation and enterprise Pega, while managing complex migration, cutover and cross-platform dependencies. 
 - Build a resilient, always-on payments capability spanning domestic and cross-border payments, real-time processing, switching, settlement, reconciliation, observability and incident readiness. 
 - Lead AI-powered engineering adoption, using generative and agentic AI for software development, testing, legacy comprehension, migration, knowledge discovery and operational support, with strong governance, responsible-use guardrails and measurable benefits. 
 - Own the India engineering operating model, including resilience, security, regulatory readiness, cost, risk, talent and capability building, while creating a high-performance culture and strong partnership across India and New Zealand. 

Essential Skills: 

- 15-18+ years of hands-on technology and engineering experience, built on a genuine engineering foundation rather than a purely programme or delivery-management career path. You should still be credible in an architecture or design review, able to read a solution design critically, and able to challenge an engineering or vendor decision on its technical merits. 
 - Deep, demonstrable delivery experience in at least one of: SAP core banking modernisation (TRBK or equivalent), Cards Modernisation, Payments, or enterprise Pega - evidenced by systems you have taken to production, not programmes you have governed. Credible working knowledge across at least two of these domains is required: depth in one is the gate, breadth is what makes this role work. 
 - Automation-first quality engineering: Proven experience building automated testing at scale across major migrations, including reusable frameworks, integration, performance, resilience and production validation, replacing manual regression with pipeline-driven automation. 
 - Core banking & legacy modernisation: Deep experience modernising complex banking platforms, including SAP HANA/core banking, large-scale data migration, reconciliation, dual-run, cutover, legacy decommissioning and AI-enabled legacy code discovery. 
 - Cards, payments & Pega expertise: Strong engineering depth across cards issuing/acquiring, payment rails and switching, settlement and reconciliation, alongside enterprise Pega platforms, workflow, decisioning and platform governance. 
 - Modern architecture & platform engineering: Strong command of cloud-native, domain-driven and event-driven architectures, microservices, APIs, distributed systems, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code and scalable platform engineering. 
 - DevSecOps, reliability & security: Advanced CI/CD, Golden Pathways, automated security controls, observability, SLOs, resilience, disaster recovery, threat modelling, vulnerability management and audit-ready technology controls. 
 - AI-powered engineering: Hands-on experience embedding agentic and generative AI across coding, code review, testing, legacy comprehension, migration and operations, with measurable outcomes, robust evaluation and responsible AI guardrails. 
 - Engineering leadership & capability building: Proven leadership of engineering leaders and multidisciplinary teams across squads, tribes and partners, with experience building senior engineering capability, insourcing critical skills and developing succession. 
 - Executive & regulated banking leadership: Strong executive presence with experience operating across jurisdictions, managing regulatory and technology risk, and building trusted partnerships with onshore product and technology leaders in complex financial services environments. 

Education Qualification: 

- Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology or a related discipline; a postgraduate technology or leadership qualification is desirable. 
 - Certifications in cloud architecture, Pega, payments, test automation, security or agile delivery are advantageous. 

If you're already part of the Commonwealth Bank Group (including Bankwest, x15ventures), you'll need to apply through Sidekick to submit a valid application. We're keen to support you with the next step in your career. 

We're aware of some accessibility issues on this site, particularly for screen reader users. We want to make finding your dream job as easy as possible, so if you require additional support please contact HR Direct on 1800 989 696.
